title: Low-Code No-Code Adoption 2026
description: Low-Code and No-Code Adoption 2026: how citizen development is expanding, where low-code platforms stand, and what buyers should consider when adopting them.
keyFindings: The low-code and no-code segment shows 28% year-over-year growth in 2026
Enterprise adoption of low-code and no-code solutions increased by 47% compared to last year
77% of organizations report improved outcomes after implementing low-code and no-code platforms
Small and medium businesses account for 52% of low-code and no-code platform spending
AI-powered features are the top consideration for 62% of buyers evaluating low-code and no-code platforms
Cloud-based deployment represents 85% of new low-code and no-code installations
Integration capabilities influence 81% of purchasing decisions
low-code and no-code platform budgets increased by an average of 26% in 2026

sections.title: The Fastest-Growing Segment
sections.body: Low-code and no-code grew 28% year over year in our 2026 data, the fastest of any segment we track. The platforms span internal app builders, workflow automation, and citizen data tools. The appeal is consistent: teams can deliver working software and automations without waiting on scarce engineering capacity.

sections.title: Adoption Patterns
sections.body: Enterprise adoption of low-code and no-code solutions increased 47% compared to last year. Adoption is spreading beyond IT: operations, finance, and HR teams now build their own workflow apps. Successful programs pair a central governance team with clear guardrails on what citizen developers can build and publish.

sections.title: Spending Patterns
sections.body: Small and medium businesses account for 52% of low-code and no-code spending, and budgets grew by an average of 26% in 2026. Pricing combines per-developer seats with usage tiers for execution runs. Buyers should model costs as automation scales, since runtime consumption can outweigh seat costs quickly.

sections.title: What Buyers Evaluate
sections.body: AI-powered features are the top consideration for 62% of buyers evaluating low-code platforms, including app generation from prompts and assisted workflow design. Integration capabilities influence 81% of purchasing decisions: the platform is only useful if it connects to the databases, APIs, and SaaS tools the organization already runs.

sections.title: Regional Deployment Patterns
sections.body: Cloud-based deployment represents 85% of new low-code installations. The category is cloud-native across regions, with governance features such as data-loss prevention and audit logs becoming table stakes. Teams in regulated industries favor platforms with enterprise controls and residency options.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.body: Define the governance model before rollout: who can build, what data is in scope, and how apps get reviewed. Pilot with one department and one defined workflow, measuring delivery time against the alternative. Review the platform annually, especially how AI-assisted building changes the developer experience and governance needs.

methodology: This research is based on a survey of 2991 IT decision-makers, analysis of 169 software vendors, and secondary research from industry analysts. Data was collected in Q1-Q2 2026.
author: PilotStack Research Team
